f1_leg_retraction.reason: scripts/a02_judge_openweight.py:423-445 REIMPLEMENTED F1 instead of importing the canonical compute_f1/normalize_answer from eval_qcmem_locomo.py:313-343. Two bugs: (1) normalize_answer operation order swapped -- canonical does remove_punc THEN remove_articles, the re-run does remove_articles THEN remove_punc, so \b(a|an|the)\b lands on different word boundaries while punctuation is still present ('the-house' -> canonical 'thehouse' vs re-run 'house'; 'a.k.a. Bob' -> 'aka bob' vs 'k bob'; 'an-apple' -> 'anapple' vs 'apple'). (2) zero-overlap: canonical returns 0.0, the re-run `continue`s.
f1_leg_retraction.canonical_value: +0.20pp CI[-0.36,+0.75] -- a TIE. This is the value to cite, because it is the F1 definition every other LoCoMo number in this project used.
f1_leg_retraction.principle: using a different normaliser for one cell of a comparison table makes cross-row comparison meaningless regardless of which normaliser is better in the abstract

storage_readcompute_reframe_gate.verdict: STORAGE FORM: DEAD. READ-COMPUTE FORM: SURVIVES WEAKLY.
storage_readcompute_reframe_gate.headline: Finite N* exists vs the phase-1 C1 arm (0.13-0.38 queries, 12/12 cells within the pre-registered 1e5 bar), BUT 86-93% of that win is RETRIEVAL, which plain text-RAG gets for free. Against a matched-pack text-RAG control, CoMem's own contribution is 1.03-1.37x per-query, needing N*=8-226 queries to repay its Write, at 2048x the bytes/token of raw text.

crossover_n_star.vs_phase1_C1_pack_all: 32k: 0.35-0.38 | 128k: 0.13 | 1M: N/A (C1 arm OOMs, 88.3GB peak) -- recorded as ARM-ABSENT, explicitly NOT as infinite N* and NOT as a CoMem win
crossover_n_star.vs_matched_pack_text_RAG: 32k: 8.1-11.9 | 128k: 25.2-42.6 | 1M: 185.5-225.5; grows ~linearly in L because Write is O(L) while the per-query saving is constant -> break-even gets WORSE for the big corpora the method is pitched at

latency_decomposition_128k_gpu_G1_ms.j0_top12: select 117.7 + fetch 0.02 + read 938.4 + decode 0.0 = 1056.2 (read_len 6177, SAME pack)
latency_decomposition_128k_gpu_G1_ms.what_the_memory_removes: the bottom-12-layer prefill: read 938.4 -> 677.9 ms = 1.38x on the read component, 1.33x on the per-query total
latency_decomposition_128k_gpu_G1_ms.G_decay: CoMem-specific per-query speedup 1.33x (G=1) -> 1.11x (G=32) -> 1.03x (G=128); decode is identical across arms so larger G dilutes the advantage to within 3%
latency_decomposition_128k_gpu_G1_ms.NEW_FINDING_selection_cost: iter_bm25 selection is O(L) on CPU per query and CoMem does NOT remove it: 17.1 ms @32k, 117.7 ms @128k, 1014.8 ms @1M = 59.9% of CoMem's entire per-query budget at 1M and LARGER than its 678 ms read. Any 'CoMem per-query cost is constant in L' claim is false once selection is counted. The published P1.8 crossover let this cancel because both its arms retrieved.

storage_readcompute_reframe_gate.quality_not_held_fixed: 'Same quality, better cost' does NOT hold, so even the weak read-compute win is not free. This gate holds selector fixed at iter_bm25 and separates depth from retrieval via a 2-hop single-variable chain (comem -> j0_top12 -> c1_all). REMAINING confound: depth and LoRA move together (irreducible -- j=12 without the Read-LoRA is not a functional arm). NOT resolved: whether phase-1's quality losses are depth failures or retrieval-recall failures.
unverified: single example / single task (niah_multikey_1, example_index=0, read_sample_length=32k); 3 procs x 5 repeats; no cross-task variance (matches released P1.8 protocol)

store tail beyond the real 32k sample is random-token padding; BM25 select time over random tokens may not match real text -- the 1014.8 ms @1M select is the least-confident number and it is load-bearing
c1_all @1M is an OOM, not a timing: its per-query cost at 1M is unmeasured; only 'does not fit in 97.8 GB' is established
no NVMe / networked storage tier measured (only gpu-resident + cpu-pinned); scripts/bench_persistent_store_io.py exists for this and was NOT run
batch=1 single-stream, no continuous batching / paged attention; a served RAG system amortises prefill across concurrent requests, further eroding a 1.33x single-stream advantage

storage_readcompute_reframe_gate.promotion_impact: Does NOT clear A02 for promotion to paper<X>. Recommended positioning: not a storage method and not a large serving win; the defensible claim is 'given you are already doing retrieval, caching mid-depth residuals removes the bottom-12-layer prefill for 1.03-1.37x per-query, repaid after ~8-226 queries/corpus, at a 2048x storage premium over raw text and with a measurable accuracy cost on long-context single-span retrieval' = a systems micro-optimisation, not a paper thesis.
